modules.title: Introduction to Judges and the Demand for a King
modules.html:
Deborah, Gideon and Samson lead Israel; the people demand a king; Saul is anointed and later rejected. This section covers introduction to judges and the demand for a king.

Key points

  • The Egyptian king who 'did not know Joseph' oppressed the Israelites because _____. — they were multiplying too fast.
  • The first king of Israel was _____. — Saul.
  • Nebuchadnezzar was the king of _____ who destroyed Jerusalem. — Babylon.
  • Daniel and his three friends refused to eat the King's meat because it _____. — was defiled.
  • Saul was rejected as king over Israel primarily because of his _____. — disobedience to God's command regarding the Amalekites.

Worked examples

Q: The Egyptian king who 'did not know Joseph' oppressed the Israelites because _____.
A: they were multiplying too fast — The King feared that the Israelites were becoming more numerous and powerful than the Egyptians (Exodus 1:9-10).

Q: The first king of Israel was _____.
A: Saul — Saul, the son of Kish, was anointed by Samuel as the first king following the people's demand.

examples.q: The Egyptian king who 'did not know Joseph' oppressed the Israelites because _____.
The first king of Israel was _____.

quiz.q: The Egyptian king who 'did not know Joseph' oppressed the Israelites because _____.
quiz.solution: The King feared that the Israelites were becoming more numerous and powerful than the Egyptians (Exodus 1:9-10).

quiz.q: The first king of Israel was _____.
quiz.solution: Saul, the son of Kish, was anointed by Samuel as the first king following the people's demand.

quiz.q: Nebuchadnezzar was the king of _____ who destroyed Jerusalem.
quiz.solution: Babylon, under Nebuchadnezzar, captured Jerusalem and took the Jews into exile.

quiz.q: Daniel and his three friends refused to eat the King's meat because it _____.
quiz.solution: The food was likely offered to idols or was not prepared according to Jewish dietary laws (kosher).

quiz.q: Saul was rejected as king over Israel primarily because of his _____.
options: disobedience to God's command regarding the Amalekites
quiz.solution: 1 Samuel 15 records that Saul spared Agag and the best of the livestock, violating God's command of total destruction (herem).

quiz.q: The king of Babylon who destroyed Jerusalem and took the people into exile was _____.
quiz.solution: Nebuchadnezzar II led the siege that resulted in the burning of the Temple and the deportation of the Jews to Babylon.

quiz.q: The prophet who challenged King Ahab and Queen Jezebel was _____.
quiz.solution: Elijah was the fierce opponent of the cult of Baal introduced by Jezebel in the Northern Kingdom.
